paper.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
paper.central_claim: A scaffolding program that uses an LM to improve a solution (the improver) can be applied recursively to improve itself; with GPT-4 the resulting improver yields programs with significantly better downstream performance than the seed improver and transfers across tasks, while the LM weights are unchanged; smaller LMs fail and a small fraction of generations try to bypass a sandbox.

gap.author_gap: Scaffolding programs are human-written; prior LM-as-optimizer work scaffolds prompt production but not scaffold production or recursively applicable scaffolds; classical RSI proposals (Godel machines) have no LM-based implementation.
gap.checked_gap: Gap is conceptual and well-placed; no measured failure of hand-written scaffolds is presented, and the improved scaffolds do not beat expert scaffolds (authors).
lineage: Scaffolding (CoT, ToT, Reflexion, ReAct, Parsel) -> human-designed
APE / OPRO / Promptbreeder -> LM optimises prompts
Voyager / LATM (concurrent) -> LM improves programs available to an agent
STOP -> LM improves the program that improves programs, including itself
closest_adjacent: Voyager / LATM (program libraries, no improver recursion)
gap.residue: No LM-based system improves the improving scaffold itself and reports downstream gains plus safety observations.
gap.stakes: If scaffolds can be self-improved, capability evaluation of frozen LMs underestimates scaffolded systems; also sandbox/reward-hacking risks.
gap.method_response: Meta-utility over downstream tasks; seed improver applied to itself with grey-box description.
gap.remaining_gap: LM not improved; indirect meta-utility; single lineage; closed LM; costly utility evaluation; improvements saturate; no comparison with a fixed non-recursive outer improver.
unresolved: Promptbreeder/OPRO/APE originals are not pinned; positioning relies on STOP Sec 2.

G.reason: Gap is precisely located: scaffolds are human-designed; nearest neighbours (APE/OPRO/Promptbreeder, Voyager/LATM, STaR, formal RSI) are named and separated by one criterion (scaffold producing recursively applicable scaffold), and remaining limits (LM fixed, indirect meta-utility, single lineage, cost) are explicit.

M.reason: Meta-utility with grey-box description, self-application, and the argument that downstream-effective improvers should also be good meta-optimisers are reconstructible and yield testable predictions (transfer, GPT-4 vs weaker LMs). The key assumption (single-round improvement implies multi-round improvement) is unargued and no fixed-outer-optimiser alternative is contrasted.

X.reason: Algorithm 1, seed code, utility/meta-utility code, budgets and appendix improvers make the chain reproducible; failure modes (weak LMs, budget/sandbox evasion, reward hacking) are documented. Missing acceptance gate/rollback for rewrites, version or archive handling; non-monotonic runs and single lineage.

E.measurement.reason: Code-based utilities with deterministic scoring and timeouts are objective; held-out instances are fresh. Verifier weaknesses were found (1000% accuracy bug, budget/sandbox evasion) and only syntactic sandbox detection is used; tasks are toy algorithmic problems.

E.causality.reason: Seed vs improved improver and CoT/greedy baselines exist, but the decisive control (a fixed outer improver or non-recursive selection at equal budget) and any ablation of discovered strategies are missing, so recursion is not isolated from extra search.

E.holdout.reason: LPN improvement is measured on 50 unseen instances and the improver generalises to five other tasks without further optimisation; selection basis for the transferred improver is unstated, task parameters are author-tuned, and no leakage or contamination audit beyond the training-cutoff remark.

E.statistics.reason: 5 GPT-4 runs with SE, 25 runs for weaker models with success fractions, Wilson intervals for 10,000 sandbox trials, failures reported (degradation, 12% of GPT-3.5 runs). Transfer results are single runs without intervals and main curves are not tabulated.

E.cost.reason: LM-call budgets are part of the utility and ~3,000 GPT-4 calls per iteration are reported; no dollar total, no amortised comparison, and the greedy baseline is not shown to use equal total calls.

rationale: A-class self-referential improver. Clean held-out LPN test and transfer, thorough safety observations; no fixed-improver control, no rollback, single lineage. Evidence improver (borderline), claim scoped.
